thread: The Barov name and seal on the grain paper: connection, not proven guilt

evidence.clue: In the overseer's stove ash: three pieces of parchment (seal-cords still through holes), the biggest with the one word left whole, 'Barov', above a seal that melted into a red blister; waybill slips 'Barov stores' and 'for Barov's factor'; a letter corner 'his lordship Barov' in a good clerk's hand. Barov on 31 of the 53 readable slips. All broken wax marked the same: a shield with something on it, gone soft.

Jaina: one of the old houses; a Lordaeron lord who sits at the King's court; they hold the land round Andorhal and, she thinks, most of the granaries; 'If they hold the granaries, their name's on the grain.' Lord Barov came to Boralus once about a timber contract and talked about wheat all through dinner.

Sylvanas: 'if Barov held the granaries, his name was on every sack that went out of them, rotten or sound'; 'Corley's master was in Andorhal till the end of the week, and nobody was going to hang Corley's master for being in Andorhal.' The overseer burned everything (dates, weights, carters, villages) not just Barov paper: a frightened man puts in the shelf unless told what to pick.

Chapter 6: shown to Arthas. He draws one slip half out with a gloved finger and reads the seal: 'That's Barov.' Jaina: 'It's on every sack in the south, good or bad. It's his granaries. I'm saying nothing about Lord Barov, only that the grain goes through Andorhal.' Arthas: 'Good. He'd sue me for the rest of it, and he'd talk for an hour first.' He knows the Barovs as a court house; no accusation was made and none taken.

notes_chapter6: Guard held: connection, not guilt. Jaina explicitly declines to accuse. Not re-explained.
readerKnows: Barov's name and seal are all over the grain paper; the overseer burned everything; the north-south sickness pattern does not map onto the granaries alone.
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas: a name; she wants it to be him and will not let herself conclude. Jaina: Barov is an old court house with granaries. Neither knows whether Barov built the plague, helped cover it, or knows nothing.
notes: Plan: connection, not proven guilt; no Mal'Ganis naming. Keep the Barov name on the table but unresolved; Chapter 6 should not assert his guilt.
